title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-p19p: Python EDHOC TH_3 uses ciphertext_2 not plaintext_2, TH_4 missing CRED_I
description:
## Summary

Python's EdhocInitiator.msg2_reception and EdhocResponder.msg2_processing compute TH_3 and TH_4 with wrong data, diverging from RFC 9528 and the Rust implementation.

## TH_3 Bug (both initiator and responder)

Per RFC 9528 §3.5: TH_3 = H(TH_2, PLAINTEXT_2, CRED_R)

Python uses:
- `ciphertext_2` instead of `plaintext_2` (line 425/627: `cbor2.dumps(ciphertext_2)`)
- `id_cred_r` instead of `cred_r` (line 427/629: `cbor2.dumps(id_cred_r)`)

The id_cred_r vs cred_r difference is benign for raw-key credentials (both are same 32-byte value), but ciphertext_2 vs plaintext_2 produces a different hash.

## TH_4 Bug (both initiator and responder)

Per RFC 9528 §3.5: TH_4 = H(TH_3, PLAINTEXT_3, CRED_I)

Python uses:
- `ciphertext_3` instead of `plaintext_3` (line 448/683)
- Missing `cred_i` entirely — TH_4 hash is computed over only 2 items instead of 3

## Rust Reference

Rust correctly uses:
- `transcript_3(th_2, plaintext_2, credential_r)` at lines 1151, 1477
- `transcript_4(th_3, plaintext_3, credential_i)` at lines 1199, 1629

## Impact

Python and Rust EDHOC implementations produce different OSCORE contexts, breaking cross-implementation interop (P0 requirement per AGENTS.md).
